$description: screamingface — canonical design tokens for the honest-AGI initiative. SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH. Edit here, then `node build.mjs` to regenerate dist/. Never hand-edit dist/*. Standalone OpenMined brand system — self-contained, no external design-system dependency.

color.$description: SFDS v2 — GENERATION CONFIG, not literal values. build.mjs feeds this whole block to tokens/color-gen.mjs (zero-dep OKLCH engine, ported from the round-2-final Python generator) which SOLVES the full 12-step scale per family per mode, the semantic themes, the data-viz scales, the gradient, and the alpha overlays. Model: 12-step role-per-step (Radix-class) — 1-8 backgrounds/borders (fixed OKLab-L profile per mode), 9 solid (hue's chroma-cusp L, binary-searched argmax in-gamut chroma), 10 hover-solid (cusp nudged), 11/12 text (L solved by APCA bisection against step-2 bg, targets 75/90 (low raised from 60, 2026-07-17 — legibility is the brand: text-low must clear ~4.5:1 WCAG at small sizes on both grounds)). Chroma follows a parabola peaking at step 9, tapered in dark mode. A small deliberate hue rotation runs across the ramp. Neutral is near-achromatic (fixed tiny chroma, no cusp/parabola). Edit values here to retune the system; never hand-edit dist/tokens.css.

gold.$note: brand + the one 'gain/SOTA/winner' hue. Marketing-theme accent.

blue.$note: App-theme accent + info. Raw seed hue nudged toward a softened, confident true-blue (the un-nudged hue overshot into dark electric indigo).

amber.$note: warning. Hue is FORCED to gold's computed hue + 18deg (not its own seed hue) so it reads as a warm gold-amber (golder than the old +28.3 lemon) while staying a visible step off brand gold so warning never collides with brand.

neutral.$note: Near-achromatic cool with per-theme temperature (one base direction per theme): LIGHT chromaLight 0.004 reads as clean near-white / neutral-grey (a barely-there cool), DARK chromaDark 0.010 reads as a clear cool blue-black. H255 both. Cool ground + warm gold accent. Was warm (H85) → uniform-cool (0.010) → per-theme, 2026-07-17.

solidChromaCap.$note: Chroma cap (fraction of cusp chroma) for the step-9/10 solid, tuned against the APCA foreground contract below. Default (unlisted families) = 1.0, i.e. unchanged cusp-chroma solid. green + amber capped so their solids don't glow neon next to the grounded red/blue (green + yellow go electric at full cusp chroma).

solidLDelta.$note: Small L 'darken' (positive) or 'lighten' (negative) nudge off the cusp for the step-9 solid. gold: small darken to clear the black-text >=60 contract with margin. blue: cusp-L solid was too dark (white-text APCA ~90) — a negative delta lightens it into a brighter true-blue landing white-text APCA ~62-68. blue DARK goes further (-0.15): a lighter dark-mode blue flips the fg contract to BLACK text (APCA ~60 vs white ~49; WCAG 6.7 vs 3.1) — dark text on the dark-mode primary, per Bennett 2026-07-17. green: darken off the very-light cusp so success reads as a grounded green, not neon.

lowOverride.$note: Documented brand exception: gold accent text on LIGHT targets Lc 62 (APCA fluent-text floor) — at Lc 75 gold is forced so dark it reads umber regardless of chroma; the brand accent must READ gold. Dark keeps 75 (gold-on-dark is luminous anyway). Consumers compensate with semibold at small sizes.

textChromaBoost.$note: Per-family chroma multiplier for the step-11 text-low solve (gamut-clamped, contrast-neutral: APCA still solves L). Gold at Lc 75 drifted BROWN at base chroma — the boost restores hue identity so gold text reads gold, not umber.

roleSteps.$description: Semantic action-role -> primitive step, applied per family (action) and for the neutral structural ladder (neutral). This is what themes below alias.

themes.$description: Role -> family map. Both themes draw from the identical 12-step primitives; only the role->family mapping differs. app = product/UI (accent=blue, the cool interactive hue). marketing = brand-forward pages (accent=gold, brand leads as hero). build.mjs emits `app` to :root/[data-theme=dark] by default and overrides ONLY the accent-family aliases under [data-brand=marketing].

data.$description: Data-viz palettes. categoricalPairs are literal anchor hexes (light=@600, dark=@400 verbatim; the 5-step ramp interpolates 300/500/700 from these two). sequential/diverging are DERIVED from the family primitives above (hue + cusp chroma), not literal.

categoricalPairs.$note: 10 hues, CVD-validated (dataviz skill): worst adjacent min(protan,deutan) ΔE 9.2 light / 9.4 dark (target 8), normal-vision ΔE >=16, all chroma >=0.10, no purple (280-330 vacated), gold-band vacated so it never collides with brand gold. Order is CVD-safe adjacency (brute-forced). teal/cyan run bright in light mode (contrast <3:1 on white) so chart series must carry a visible label/table — enforced in the data-viz examples. Regenerate via scratchpad gen-dataviz.mjs.

diverging.$note: the 'gain over SOTA' below/above-baseline encoding; two constant hues only (never interpolated through the circle, so it can't pass through purple), chroma tapers to ~0 at the shared light-neutral center

gradient.$description: The single sanctioned SFDS gradient token (fusion-grad): a symmetric gold → luminous near-white → blue sweep mirroring the 😱 (gold face · white middle · blue crown). OKLCH-interpolated over 32 stops so it stays smooth on large fills. Hue holds gold across the warm half and blue across the cool half; the near-neutral center masks the switch, so no green and no purple ever appear. dawn + baseline are intentionally NOT wired.

fusionGrad.note: Gold → luminous near-white bridge → blue. Chroma dips to near-zero at the center while LIGHTNESS peaks, so it reads as a clean glow, not a muddy gray. Symmetric, emoji-faithful.

alpha.$note: neutral = black-on-light / white-on-dark overlay tints. accent-<theme> = that theme's accent-9 solid, tinted — for hover/scrim/overlay use.

font.$description: display = Parastoo (marketing headlines — warm editorial serif, the expressive voice). sans = IBM Plex Sans (the load-bearing product/UI + body). mono = IBM Plex Mono (data, labels, code, receipts, the rail). wordmark = Plex Sans 600 tight (the quiet, engineered lockup; Rubik retired). All self-hosted (brand-site/fonts.css) — no external font CDN.

display.$value: "Parastoo", "Iowan Old Style", Georgia, "Times New Roman", serif
display.$description: Marketing headlines / h1. Parastoo (Saber Rastikerdar, OFL) — a warm editorial serif for the expressive marketing register. The sans (IBM Plex Sans) does the load-bearing product/UI work. Self-hosted, 4 static weights (400–700).

mono.$value: "IBM Plex Mono", ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, monospace

wordmark.$description: The screamingface wordmark/logo lockup only — Plex Sans set tight (medium at display sizes, semibold at rail size). Rubik retired 2026-07-15. Not for UI or body type.

size.$description: Layout constants, not part of the color theme.

text.$description: Type scale — one font-size per role. Compose with --f-*, --weight-*, --tracking-*, --leading-*. Eight roles, deliberately few. Two registers share one scale: MARKETING leads with hero/display in Parastoo; PRODUCT tops out at display and is carried by Sans + Mono.

hero.$description: marketing hero headline only (Parastoo). Fluid; never in product UI.

title.$description: section sub-heads / card titles (Sans semibold or Parastoo 500)

label.$description: ALL uppercase labels: eyebrow, kickers, table headers, kv keys (Mono 500, tracking-label). One weight, one tracking — the single caps treatment. (h2 is no longer a label — it's a sans display heading.)

display.$description: serif display (Parastoo) at hero/display sizes — MEDIUM, its stroke contrast carries the mass. Sans titles/headings stay semibold. Decided 2026-07-16 on the guide masthead; written back per the round-trip rule.

label.$description: the single tracking for all caps labels

hero.$description: hero/display serif only. OPTICALLY set for Parastoo: its Perso-Arabic vertical metrics leave Latin caps small in a tall em, so numeric 1.05 reads loose — 0.98 lands the classic tight display look.

snug.$description: deks/leads — tightened optically for 18-20px Plex Sans

space.$description: 4px-based spacing scale for padding, margin, gap.

radius.$description: The system is square. Radius is 0, on purpose (see anti-rules) — with ONE sanctioned exception: window-chrome frames.

window.$description: window-chrome frames ONLY (.note terminal boxes). Decided 2026-07-16: a terminal window without rounded corners does not read as a terminal window. 10px matches macOS.

shadow.$description: The system is FLAT — depth from spacing and rules (see anti-rules). ONE sanctioned exception: floating window chrome.

window.$description: window-chrome (.note terminal), LIGHT mode — soft, diffuse, cool-tinted low-alpha elevation (a heavy black shadow reads stark on a near-white page).

window-dark.$description: window-chrome, DARK mode — the deeper macOS-like ambient+key shadow that reads as depth on a dark ground. Applied via [data-theme=dark] .note.

terminal.$description: The 'macOS terminal' chrome (.note window) as an ELEVATED NEUTRAL surface — same cool-neutral family as the whole page (not a separate blue), so it never out-tints the ground. It reads as a terminal via elevation (shadow) + a crisp neutral edge + one surface step, and it flips with the page (light near-white card, dark cool panel). All var() refs.

bg.$description: window body — neutral surface (light near-white, dark cool panel)

chrome.$description: title bar — one neutral step off the body

line.$description: window border + title-bar seam — neutral border (crisp, not a fuzzy low-contrast tint)

dim.$description: muted TEXT in the terminal body — the secondary text role (readable; audit 2026-07-17)

deco.$description: decorative window chrome ONLY — the traffic-light dots, the title-bar label, non-winning bar fills. Deliberately quiet (Bennett 2026-07-17: chrome should recede); never for body/reading text.

accent.$description: prompt $, kv keys, receipt — gold that stays readable on both grounds
